title: "Interactive dose optimisation"
description: "Define a therapeutic target for a PKPD model and let an OptiDose-style optimiser find the dose, live in your browser."

resources:
  - pkpd.js
---

Choose a therapeutic target, and the optimiser finds the dose that fulfils it. Everything runs in your browser, so the result updates as soon as you change an input.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
This page illustrates the optimisation principle with an example model. It is not intended for clinical dosing decisions.
:::

```{ojs}
import { simulate, optimiseDose, metrics, objective, defaultParams } from "./pkpd.js"
```

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-lg-4}

#### Target

```{ojs}
// A link with ?target=pd_min|cmax_max|auc_mic preselects the target
initialTarget = {
  const t = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("target");
  return ["pd_min", "cmax_max", "auc_mic"].includes(t) ? t : "pd_min";
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof targetType = Inputs.radio(
  new Map([
    ["PD response must not fall below a threshold", "pd_min"],
    ["Peak concentration must not exceed a threshold", "cmax_max"],
    ["AUC/MIC must reach a threshold", "auc_mic"]
  ]),
  { value: initialTarget }
)
```

```{ojs}
viewof threshold = Inputs.number({
  value: { pd_min: 30, cmax_max: 4, auc_mic: 125 }[targetType],
  label: { pd_min: "Minimum PD response", cmax_max: "Maximum concentration (mg/L)", auc_mic: "Target AUC/MIC (h)" }[targetType]
})
```

```{ojs}
viewof mic = targetType === "auc_mic"
  ? Inputs.number({ value: 1, label: "MIC (mg/L)", min: 0.001 })
  : Object.assign(html`<span>`, { value: 1 })
```

```{ojs}
viewof win = Inputs.form({
  from: Inputs.number({ value: 0, label: "Evaluate from (h)", min: 0 }),
  to: Inputs.number({ value: targetType === "auc_mic" ? 24 : 200, label: "Evaluate to (h)", min: 1 })
})
```

#### Dosing regimen

```{ojs}
viewof regimen = Inputs.form({
  nDoses: Inputs.range([1, 10], { value: 1, step: 1, label: "Number of doses" }),
  interval: Inputs.range([4, 72], { value: 24, step: 4, label: "Dosing interval (h)" })
})
```

```{ojs}
viewof doseMax = Inputs.number({ value: 200, label: "Search doses up to (mg)", min: 1 })
```

<details class="model-params">
<summary>Model parameters</summary>

```{ojs}
viewof modelParams = Inputs.form({
  tlag: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.tlag.toFixed(3), label: "Lag time (h)", min: 0 }),
  ka: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.ka.toFixed(3), label: "ka (1/h)", min: 0.001 }),
  V: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.V.toFixed(3), label: "V (L)", min: 0.01 }),
  CL: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.CL.toFixed(4), label: "CL (L/h)", min: 0.0001 }),
  R0: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.R0.toFixed(2), label: "Baseline response R0", min: 0 }),
  kout: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.kout.toFixed(4), label: "kout (1/h)", min: 0.0001 }),
  Imax: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.Imax.toFixed(3), label: "Imax", min: 0, max: 1 }),
  IC50: Inputs.number({ value: +defaultParams.IC50.toFixed(3), label: "IC50 (mg/L)", min: 0.001 })
})
```

One-compartment PK with first-order absorption and lag time; indirect-response PD with inhibition of production: $\frac{dR}{dt} = k_{in}\left(1 - \frac{I_{max} C}{C + IC_{50}}\right) - k_{out} R$, with $k_{in} = R_0 k_{out}$.

</details>

:::
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-lg-8}

```{ojs}
target = ({ type: targetType, threshold, from: win.from, to: win.to, mic })
tEnd = Math.max(win.to, (regimen.nDoses - 1) * regimen.interval + 48)
opt = optimiseDose(regimen, modelParams, target, tEnd, doseMax)
simOpt = simulate(opt.dose, regimen, modelParams, tEnd)
mOpt = metrics(simOpt, target)
feasible = objective(simOpt, target).constraint < 1e-3
```

```{ojs}
function summary(m) {
  if (targetType === "pd_min") return `lowest PD response ${m.minR.toFixed(1)} (target ≥ ${threshold})`;
  if (targetType === "cmax_max") return `peak concentration ${m.cmax.toFixed(2)} mg/L at ${m.tmax.toFixed(1)} h (target ≤ ${threshold})`;
  return `AUC/MIC ${m.aucMic.toFixed(1)} h (target ≥ ${threshold})`;
}
```

```{ojs}
html`<div class="opt-result">
  <div class="opt-label">Optimal dose${regimen.nDoses > 1 ? ` per administration (${regimen.nDoses} × every ${regimen.interval} h)` : ""}</div>
  <div class="opt-dose">${opt.dose.toFixed(1)} mg</div>
  <div class="opt-detail">${summary(mOpt)}, evaluated ${win.from}–${win.to} h</div>
  ${opt.atBound ? html`<div class="opt-warn">The optimum lies at the search limit. Increase "Search doses up to".</div>` : ""}
  ${!feasible ? html`<div class="opt-warn">The target cannot be met with this model and regimen; the dose shown violates it least.</div>` : ""}
</div>`
```

```{ojs}
viewof cmpDose = Inputs.range([0, doseMax], { value: Math.round(opt.dose * 10) / 10, step: 0.1, label: "Compare with dose (mg)" })
```

```{ojs}
simCmp = simulate(cmpDose, regimen, modelParams, tEnd)
mCmp = metrics(simCmp, target)
html`<div class="opt-detail">Comparison dose: ${summary(mCmp)}</div>`
```

```{ojs}
function rows(sim, series, key) {
  const out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < sim.time.length; i += 5) out.push({ time: sim.time[i], value: sim[key][i], series });
  return out;
}
colors = ({ domain: ["Optimal dose", "Comparison dose"], range: ["#a349a4", "#8a8f98"] })

function panel(key, ylabel, rule) {
  return Plot.plot({
    width,
    height: 240,
    marginLeft: 55,
    x: { label: "Time (h)", domain: [0, tEnd] },
    y: { label: ylabel, grid: true, zero: true },
    color: { ...colors, legend: true },
    marks: [
      Plot.rectX([{ x1: win.from, x2: Math.min(win.to, tEnd) }], { x1: "x1", x2: "x2", fill: "currentColor", fillOpacity: 0.06 }),
      key === "conc" && targetType === "auc_mic"
        ? Plot.areaY(rows(simOpt, "Optimal dose", key).filter((d) => d.time >= win.from && d.time <= win.to),
            { x: "time", y: "value", fill: "#a349a4", fillOpacity: 0.18 })
        : null,
      rule === undefined ? null : Plot.ruleY([rule], { stroke: "#e8590c", strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeDasharray: "6,4" }),
      Plot.line(rows(simCmp, "Comparison dose", key), { x: "time", y: "value", stroke: "series", strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "4,3" }),
      Plot.line(rows(simOpt, "Optimal dose", key), { x: "time", y: "value", stroke: "series", strokeWidth: 2.5 }),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
panel("conc", "Concentration (mg/L)", targetType === "cmax_max" ? threshold : undefined)
```

```{ojs}
targetType === "auc_mic" ? html`` : panel("resp", "PD response", targetType === "pd_min" ? threshold : undefined)
```

```{ojs}
md`${targetType === "auc_mic"
  ? "The grey band is the evaluation window; the purple area is the AUC compared with the target (AUC/MIC)."
  : "The grey band is the evaluation window; the dashed orange line is the threshold."}`
```

:::
:::

## How the optimiser works

Following the [OptiDose](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.6188) approach, the target is turned into a penalty: violating it costs a lot, and a much smaller secondary term makes the answer unique. For a lower limit on the PD response or an upper limit on the peak concentration, the secondary term rewards exposure, so the optimiser finds the *highest* dose that still respects the limit. For AUC/MIC, it penalises exposure, so the optimiser finds the *lowest* dose that reaches the target. The optimiser scans the dose range and then refines the minimum with a golden-section search.

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width,
  height: 220,
  marginLeft: 55,
  x: { label: "Dose (mg)" },
  y: { label: "Penalty (log scale)", type: "log", grid: true },
  marks: [
    Plot.line(opt.landscape, { x: "dose", y: (d) => d.objective + 1e-4, stroke: "currentColor" }),
    Plot.ruleX([opt.dose], { stroke: "#a349a4", strokeWidth: 2 }),
    Plot.text([opt.dose], { x: (d) => d, frameAnchor: "top", dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", text: (d) => `optimum ${d.toFixed(1)} mg`, fill: "#a349a4" })
  ]
})
```

In pharmacometric software, [optiDoseR](../tutorials/optiDoseR/index.qmd) sets up the same idea for Monolix, NONMEM, and nlmixr2, where the dose is *estimated* together with the model, including individual doses for patients with inter-individual variability.
